oracle_provenance: Plain additive arithmetic checked against the well-known ITU-T G.114 150 ms one-way conversational-quality guideline; independently hand-verified before implementation. Not copied from any shared Skill fixture.
scope: Bounded additive one-way audio latency budget checked against the ITU-T G.114 150 ms threshold; not a measured end-to-end latency on real hardware/network.

cases.question: When the summed latency budget comes to 155 ms, does it correctly exceed the 150 ms ITU-T G.114 recommendation by exactly 5 ms?
With a leaner jitter buffer and network path, does the total latency stay within the 150 ms guideline?
Must a negative delay component be rejected rather than silently used?
Does the reported per-stage breakdown sum exactly to the reported total, discriminating a genuine additive model from a rounding artifact?
